sentences.text: Pepesuchus possessed a roughly triangular skull covered in small pits when viewed from above. Its jaws were lined with many small, pointed teeth that were laterally compressed and serrated.
This animal had 17 teeth in each maxilla, which is the highest count among sebecians after Stolokrosuchus.

The genus name Pepesuchus honors Professor José Martin Suárez, nicknamed "Pepe", and combines it with the Greek word for crocodile. The species name deiseae honors the paleontologist Deise Dias Rêgo Henriques.
Its ziphodont teeth were laterally compressed and serrated, a specialized adaptation for its feeding style.
Pepesuchus was named by a team of researchers including Diogenes A. Campos and Alexander W.A. Kellner in 2011.

Pepesuchus is classified within the family Peirosauridae and belongs to the parent group Pepesuchinae. It is grouped with the peirosaurids Peirosaurus, Lomasuchus, and Uberabasuchus based on shared characteristics.

Pepesuchus was a semiaquatic crocodylomorph that lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the state of São Paulo, Brazil. This creature lived from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
